target.scientificName: Macaca munzala Sinha, Datta, Madhusudan & Mishra, 2005

sourceReuse.rightsEvidenceLocator: PLOS copyright statement states the article is open access under a Creative Commons Attribution license and links to CC BY 4.0.

claim.text: The mitochondrial-DNA Bayesian skyline plot for the tentative Upper Subansiri population indicated expansion after the Last Glacial Maximum, around 15,000 years before present. This is a model-inferred trajectory for one geographically distinct population, based on 10 successfully sequenced individuals from 12 Upper Subansiri trophy-skin samples; the study could not rule out effects of local migrants. It does not estimate census size or establish a species-wide history. The same plot's small apparent reduction 5,000–7,000 years ago may fall within the credibility interval and was not treated as conclusive evidence of a demographic shift.
claim.textZh: 基于线粒体 DNA 的贝叶斯天际线图显示，Upper Subansiri 暂定种群在末次盛冰期之后、约 15,000 年前出现扩张。这是对一个地理上独立种群的模型推断；Upper Subansiri 的 12 份旧狩猎战利品皮样本中有 10 份成功测序，研究也无法排除局部迁入者对结果的影响。该结果不估算普查数量，也不能外推为整个物种的种群史。同一图中 5,000–7,000 年前轻微下降可能位于可信区间内，因此不能视为确定的人口变化证据。
claim.locator: Bayesian skyline plot methods and results (article lines 177-182 and 224-236); sample size and successful sequencing (lines 167-175); geographically distinct populations and unsampled-migration limitation (lines 225-229); caution about interpreting the later small reduction (lines 228-229).
claim.placeTimeScope: Tentative Upper Subansiri population, Arunachal Pradesh, northeastern India; mitochondrial-DNA Bayesian skyline analysis published in 2014. Ten individuals were successfully sequenced from 12 trophy-skin samples for that population.
claim.lifeStatus: Historical demographic inference from mtDNA of sampled wild animals whose skins came from old hunting trophies; the wider study's captive Tawang blood sample is outside this Upper Subansiri claim.

completenessReasons: Two model-based demographic results in one study concern the tentative Upper Subansiri population; neither estimates present-day census size or the demographic history of the full species range.

The mtDNA skyline expansion near 15,000 years before present and the separate microsatellite ABC decline estimate near 3,500 years before present depend on limited samples and do not resolve unsampled migration or causal drivers.
Morphology, life history, other ecology, range-wide distribution, fossils, conservation status, systematic evidence search, and external expert review remain unassessed.
